school: 二十世纪后半叶实验物理的精度立法者：1936 年生于美国安阿伯（父母访美期间出生，三个月大即随父母回国），战乱中由外婆在山东、重庆带大，1948 年随家去台湾，1955 年入成功中学，1956 年以全班状元的成绩保送台湾大学历史系，一年后弃文转工，考入台湾大学电机系又转物理系；1956 年 8 月只带 100 美元赴美国密歇根大学自费留学，三年拿下数学与物理双学位，1960 年获物理学博士——从到达美国到获得博士学位仅用六年；1963 年赴哥伦比亚大学任讲师，1966 年到德国汉堡 DESY 用一年的时间以比哈佛实验高十倍的精度重测电子半径，否定了哈佛小组'电子有半径'的结论，一战成名；1969 年任麻省理工学院教授，此后数十年主持 MIT 第 24 号实验室；1974 年 8 月起在布鲁克海文国家实验室的 30 GeV 质子同步加速器上以'把亿分之一的信号从海量本底中挑出'的双臂谱仪系统搜索长寿命中性矢量介子，同年 11 月 10 日确认质量 3.1 GeV 的新粒子——几乎同时里希特在 SLAC 的正负电子对撞机上独立发现同一粒子，物理学史称'十一月革命'，两人同获 1976 年诺贝尔物理学奖；1975 年起领导 Mark-J 国际合作组在汉堡 PETRA 对撞机上精确检验量子电动力学，证明电子、μ 子、τ 轻子在 10^-16 厘米尺度仍为点粒子；1982 年起主持 LEP 上的 L3 实验——上千名物理学家、19 个国家、43 所大学参加，是当时最大的国际科学合作；1994 年 60 岁时提出把磁谱仪（AMS）送上国际空间站寻找反物质与暗物质——被权威评委判为'不可能'，他组建 16 个国家、60 余所大学与研究所、数百名科学家的国际合作，1998 年 AMS-01 搭'发现号'航天飞机首飞，2011 年 5 月 AMS-02 由'奋进号'最后一个航班送上空间站，此后在轨道运行十余年、收集上千亿个宇宙线事例，发表正电子分数、反氦搜索、宇宙线流强等一批重要结果；他反复强调'基础研究是新技术与工业发展的原动力'，坚持每个实验都亲自验收、从不假手于人——他证明：实验物理学家最重要的素质是'对自己要有信心，做你认为正确的事'，而精度本身就是科学
historical_significance: 丁肇中（Samuel C. C. Ting，1936- ），1936 年 1 月 27 日生于美国密歇根州安阿伯，父母当时在密歇根大学访问，三个月大即随父母回到中国；童年与少年在战乱中度过，由外婆抚养，曾在山东日照老家读私塾，后随家迁居台湾；1955 年高中毕业时成绩全班第一，被保送台湾大学历史系，但他说服父母改考工科，考入台湾大学电机系，一年后出于对物理的兴趣转入物理系；1956 年 8 月只身赴美，随身只带 100 美元，因英语不熟、经济拮据全部靠奖学金完成学业——1959 年同时获数学与工程物理双学位，1960 年获物理学博士学位，前后仅用六年（常说'我这一生只做一件事：实验物理'）；1963 年经欧本海默等推荐到哥伦比亚大学任教，1965 年到德国汉堡德国电子同步加速器研究中心（DESY）做实验：当时哈佛大学有一个实验宣布'测到电子有半径'，与量子电动力学冲突——丁肇中用远高于哈佛的精度重测，1966 年发表结果证明电子半径小于 10^-14 厘米，哈佛结论错误，这是他第一次以'精度挑战权威'成名；1967 年起在麻省理工学院任教，1969 年任正教授；1960 年代末他把全部精力投入'系统搜索新粒子'的计划：判断在质子束流中产生大质量光子然后衰变成正负电子对的过程，可能发现新的长寿命中性粒子；为排除海量本底，他设计双臂谱仪——两套独立的磁谱仪分别测量正负电子的动量，把质子本底的通过率压到亿分之一以下，又在实验前先注入已知粒子做全流程校验；1974 年夏天在布鲁克海文 30 GeV 质子同步加速器上，他在 4-5 GeV 的正负电子对不变质量谱上发现一个异常尖锐的峰；为确认不是假象，他用两种完全独立的测量与分析反复检验，直到 11 月确认无误——'J/ψ 粒子'由此诞生，几乎同时 SLAC 的里克特小组在正负电子对撞机上独立发现同一粒子，两处互证使全世界的怀疑一扫而空；这一发现使粒子物理从'三夸克'转向'第四种夸克（粲夸克）'，被称为'十一月革命'；丁肇中与里克特同获 1976 年诺贝尔物理学奖，领奖时他用中文演讲，题为《我的祖国》，讲述中国的科学传统——他说：'我是在旧中国长大，所以想借这个机会向发展中国家的青年强调实验工作的重要性'；1975 年起他组建 Mark-J 国际合作组在汉堡 PETRA 检验量子电动力学，证明轻子在 10^-16 厘米尺度仍是点粒子，并证实胶子的三喷注事例；1982 年起主持 CERN LEP 的 L3 实验，来自 19 个国家 43 所大学的上千名物理学家参加，探测器重达一万吨；1994 年他 58 岁，不顾'不可能'的评审意见，提出把大型磁谱仪 AMS 送上国际空间站，用宇宙线直接寻找反物质与暗物质——这是空间站上唯一的大型基础科学实验；AMS 由 16 个国家 60 余所大学与研究所参与，1998 年 AMS-01 随'发现号'首飞成功，2011 年 5 月 16 日 AMS-02 由'奋进号'最后一个航天航班送上空间站，运行至今收集超千亿宇宙线事例，测定正电子分数曲线、宇宙线流强谱，对暗物质给出最严格的间接限制之一；他多次公开批评'轻视基础研究'的短视：'基础研究是新技术与工业发展的原动力'；他坚持实验的每一环节亲自验收，常对年轻物理学家说：'做实验物理，第一要对自己有信心，做你认为正确的事，不要因为多数人反对而改变；第二要不断问自己，这个实验的意义是什么'；他证明：精度不是工具，精度是发现本身
historical_significance_en: Samuel C. C. Ting (born 1936) was born in Ann Arbor, Michigan, on 27 January 1936, while his parents were visiting the University of Michigan; three months later they returned with him to China. His childhood was spent amid war, raised largely by his maternal grandmother in Shandong and Chongqing; in 1948 the family moved to Taiwan. He finished high school at the top of his class in 1955 and was admitted without examination into the history department of National Taiwan University, but persuaded his parents to let him switch to engineering, entered NTU's electrical engineering program, and after a year transferred to physics out of pure interest. In August 1956 he left for the United States with one hundred dollars in his pocket, knowing little English and nearly penniless, and supported himself entirely on scholarships: by 1959 he held degrees in both mathematics and engineering physics, and in 1960 a doctorate in physics — six years from arrival to PhD ('I have done only one thing all my life: experimental physics'). In 1963, through recommendations, he became an instructor at Columbia, and in 1965 went to DESY in Hamburg: Harvard had run an experiment claiming to measure a nonzero electron radius, contradicting quantum electrodynamics — Ting re-measured with an order of magnitude more precision and in 1966 showed the electron radius is below 10^-14 cm; Harvard was wrong, and his first fame as the precision challenger of authority was made. He joined MIT in 1967 and became full professor in 1969, running Laboratory 24 for decades. In the late 1960s he committed to a systematic search for new particles, judging that high-mass photons produced in proton beams and decaying into electron-positron pairs could reveal new long-lived neutral vector particles. To crush the background he designed a double-arm spectrometer — two independent magnetic arms measuring the momenta of the positron and the electron, reducing the hadron rejection rate to below one in a hundred million — and before every physics run he injected known particles to validate the full chain. In the summer of 1974, on Brookhaven's 30 GeV proton synchrotron, he found an abnormally sharp peak in the invariant-mass spectrum of electron-positron pairs near 3.1 GeV; to rule out artifact he re-checked with two entirely independent measurements and analyses until November, when confirmation was total — the J/ψ particle was born. Nearly simultaneously Richter's group at SLAC independently found the same particle in an electron-positron collider, and the double confirmation swept away all doubt. The discovery turned particle physics from three quarks to a fourth (charm) — the 'November Revolution'. Ting and Richter shared the 1976 Nobel Prize in Physics; Ting delivered his banquet lecture in Chinese, titled 'My Motherland', telling of China's scientific tradition — 'I was raised in old China, so I want to use this occasion to stress to young people in developing countries the importance of experimental work'. From 1975 he led the international Mark-J collaboration at PETRA in Hamburg, testing quantum electrodynamics and proving leptons are pointlike down to 10^-16 cm, and confirming the three-jet gluon events. From 1982 he directed L3 at CERN's LEP — more than a thousand physicists from 19 countries and 43 universities, a ten-thousand-ton detector. In 1994, at fifty-eight, overruling review panels that judged it impossible, he proposed flying a large magnetic spectrometer, AMS, on the International Space Station to search cosmic rays directly for antimatter and dark matter — the only large fundamental-science experiment on the station. AMS grew into a collaboration of 16 countries and more than 60 universities and institutes; AMS-01 flew on Discovery in 1998, and AMS-02 rode the final shuttle flight of Endeavour to the station on 16 May 2011, operating for over a decade, collecting hundreds of billions of cosmic-ray events, measuring the positron fraction, cosmic-ray flux spectra, and setting among the strictest indirect limits on dark matter. He has repeatedly attacked the shortsightedness of undervaluing basic research: 'basic research is the driving force of new technology and industry'. He insists on personally inspecting every part of an experiment, and tells young physicists: 'in experimental physics, first, have confidence in yourself, do what you believe is right, and do not change because the majority objects; second, keep asking yourself what the significance of the experiment is'. He proved that precision is not a tool — precision is discovery itself.
unique_thinking: 丁肇中的独特处在于三重'精度的立法'：第一，权威冲突处先重测——哈佛说电子有半径，他不写论文驳斥，而是把精度提高十倍直接重测，让实验自己处决权威结论：他证明与理论冲突时，最便宜的办法不是辩论而是更准的测量；第二，本底的立法——J/ψ 的发现不是靠好运气，而是靠'亿分之一通过率'的仪器设计加'实验前先注入已知粒子校验全链路'的纪律：他证明从海量噪声里捞信号，决定性的不是运气而是事前的筛选设计；第三，宣布的纪律——发现尖峰后他不用单一分析宣布，而是等两种完全独立的测量互证之后才确认，宁可慢六周不冒错报之险，而正是这六周使 SLAC 的独立发现得以互证、'十一月革命'才立得住：他证明'只有第一，没有第二'的含义不是抢时间，而是唯一正确的那个结果；此外他把'基础研究'当成一种公理式的信念来辩护——从 J/ψ 到 AMS，他一生都在回答同一个问题：'这个实验的意义是什么'
unique_thinking_en: Ting's singularity is a triple legislation of precision. First, where authority conflicts, re-measure: when Harvard claimed a nonzero electron radius, he wrote no polemic — he re-measured with ten times the precision and let the experiment itself execute the authority's conclusion; where theory and experiment clash, the cheapest weapon is not debate but a more accurate measurement. Second, legislating the background: the discovery of the J/ψ owed nothing to luck — it came from instrument design with a rejection rate of one in a hundred million plus the discipline of injecting known particles to validate the whole chain before physics running; extracting signal from an ocean of noise is decided not by fortune but by filtering designed in advance. Third, the discipline of announcement: on finding the sharp peak he did not declare it on a single analysis, but waited until two entirely independent measurements corroborated it — six weeks slower, no risk of a false claim — and precisely those six weeks allowed SLAC's independent discovery to cross-confirm, without which the November Revolution could not have stood; 'only first place, no second' means not beating the clock but being the one correct result. Beyond this, he defends basic research as an axiomatic conviction — from the J/ψ to AMS, his whole life answers one question: 'what is the significance of this experiment?'
civilization_zh: 二十世纪六十年代至今的日内瓦、汉堡与同步辐射实验室——一个在密歇根大学靠奖学金读完博士的华人实验物理学家，用三十年时间把'测量精度'变成一种统治性武器：他在汉堡推翻哈佛的电子半径实验，在布鲁克海文的质子束流里以亿分之一的筛选率捞出 J/ψ 粒子，在 LEP 建造上千人参与的 L3 探测器，又把一台两吨重的磁谱仪送上国际空间站十六年找反物质——他就是证明'实验物理只有第一，没有第二'的人
civilization_en: Geneva, Hamburg and the particle laboratories from the 1960s to the present — a Chinese-American experimental physicist who finished his PhD on a scholarship at Michigan turned measurement precision into a ruling weapon over thirty years: he refuted Harvard's electron-radius experiment in Hamburg, fished the J/ψ particle out of a proton beam at Brookhaven with a rejection rate of one in a hundred million, built the L3 detector at LEP with over a thousand collaborators, and flew a two-ton magnetic spectrometer on the International Space Station for sixteen years hunting antimatter — the man who proved that in experimental physics there is only first place, no second
roles_zh: MIT 第 24 号实验室主持人
AMS 磁谱仪国际合作领导者
布鲁克海文 J/ψ 发现者
roles_en: Leader of the AMS spectrometer collaboration
Discoverer of the J/ψ particle at Brookhaven
key_works: 《电子半径的高精度测量》（DESY，1966，否定哈佛实验）
《发现 J/ψ 粒子》（布鲁克海文，1974，双臂谱仪实验）
《J/ψ 粒子的质量与宽度》（1975-1976 系列论文）
Mark-J 实验：量子电动力学检验与三喷注事例（PETRA，1978-1982）
《L3 探测器设计报告》（LEP，1983 起）
《AMS 在国际空间站上的宇宙线测量》（2013-2023 系列论文）

cross_references.description_zh: 丁肇中与朗道同属'标准的立法者'：朗道以理论最低标准考试立法学派的入口，丁肇中以'亿分之一本底通过率'与'实验前先校验全链路'立法实验的入口——两人都拒绝'先收进来再放宽'，不合格的数据连门都进不了；朗道的研讨班火力双向，丁肇中的仪器对自己的数据同样开刀（发现尖峰后先怀疑假象）；平行命题：一门学科的成熟，等于它入口处的筛选率——理论筛人，实验筛数据。
cross_references.description_en: Ting and Landau belong to the same family of legislators of standards: Landau legislated a school's entrance with the theoretical minimum examination, Ting legislated an experiment's entrance with a rejection rate of one in a hundred million and the pre-run validation of the whole chain — both refused to 'take them in first and relax later'; unqualified data, like unqualified students, never gets in. Landau's seminar fire ran both ways; Ting's instruments were turned on his own data as well (the sharp peak was first suspected as artifact). The parallel thesis: a discipline's maturity equals the rejection rate at its entrance — theory filters people, experiment filters data.

cross_references.description_zh: 丁肇中与爱因斯坦站在理论-实验光谱的两端：爱因斯坦相信最高工序是铅笔与纸，仪器只是理论的下游；丁肇中则证明精度本身就是发现——J/ψ 不来自任何理论的预言，AMS 的暗物质搜索至今没有理论标准答案；爱因斯坦为世界立方程，丁肇中为'怎样才算看见了'立标准；对照命题：理论家的自由在于假设，实验家的自由在于精度——两种立法者最后在'可重复性'这一点上会师。
cross_references.description_en: Ting and Einstein stand at opposite ends of the theory-experiment spectrum: Einstein held the highest operation to be pencil and paper, instruments merely downstream; Ting proved that precision itself is discovery — the J/ψ came from no theoretical prediction, and AMS's dark-matter search has no theoretical standard answer to this day. Einstein legislated equations for the world; Ting legislated the standard for what counts as 'seeing'. The contrast thesis: the theorist's freedom lies in assumptions, the experimentalist's in precision — and the two legislators meet at last on the ground of reproducibility.

cross_references.description_zh: 丁肇中与高斯代表科学家与'未发表成果'的两种关系：高斯把最深的工作藏进抽屉，等死后发表——沉默是为了体系的完美；丁肇中把每一个环节公开于国际合作——上千名物理学家、16 个国家共同验收 AMS 的每个部件，结论在同行眼前重复千百次——公开是为了让'看见'不可否认；高斯追求一次性的完美证明，丁肇中追求可被任何人重复的测量；对照命题：数学家的正确存于证明的封闭性，实验家的正确存于测量的可开放性——前者怕被看穿，后者怕别人看不见。
cross_references.description_en: Ting and Gauss represent two relations between the scientist and unpublished work: Gauss hid his deepest results in a drawer until after death — silence in service of the system's perfection; Ting exposes every link to international collaboration — a thousand physicists and 16 countries jointly inspect every part of AMS, and conclusions are repeated hundreds of times before peers — openness so that 'seeing' is undeniable. Gauss pursued the one-time perfect proof; Ting pursues the measurement anyone can repeat. The contrast thesis: the mathematician's correctness lives in the closedness of proof, the experimentalist's in the openness of measurement — the first fears being seen through, the second fears not being seen at all.
